newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Foodland's NZ retail sales down, EBIT up.
newsitem.headline: Foodland's NZ retail sales down, EBIT up.

text.p: Australian food retailer and wholesaler Foodland Associated Ltd said on Thursday sales for its New Zealand general merchandise retailer Farmers Deka were down 0.8 percent in the six months to January 31, but earnings before tax rose 35.3 percent to A$18.4 million.

Foodland earlier reported a record half-year profit of A$28.7 million for the entire Foodland group, but said retail sales in New Zealand were soft prior to and immediately following the October 12 general election last year.

It said Farmers Deka had "directed its attention to reducing costs, increasing margins and improving operating efficiencies during the six months with particular emphasis on merchandise control and range improvement".
The Deka chain continued to incur losses, but the company was accelerating the implementation of plans to address this issue, Foodland said.
Farmers Deka is New Zealand's largest general merchandise retailer, trading through 46 family stores, 13 home centre stores, three Freedom Furniture stores and 65 Deka outlets.
Foodland said Farmers Deka continued to hold approximately 47 percent of the New Zealand department store market, making it the country's largest department store business.
"It also owns and manages Retail Financial Services Ltd, New Zealand's largest non-bank consumer finance organisation which has assets in excess of NZ$330 million," Foodland said.

Retail Financial Services increased its portfolio of consumer finance receivables by 3.2 percent to NZ$321 million. Foodland said cost of borrowings improved following the successful completion of the portfolio securitisation and refinancing last year.
Plans for a refurbishment of major Farmers outlets had been developed and approved by the Foodland board.
"Capital expenditure has been allocated and the first store refurbishment will be completed early in the new fiancial year," Foodland said.
